title: React Router Core Check
description: Check your understanding of routes, links, params, nested routes, navigation, protected routes, and data router awareness.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What does client-side routing let a React app do?

options.text: Show different UI for different URLs without a full page reload
Run React only on the server

questions.explanation: React Router maps URL state to UI while keeping the single-page app experience.

questions.prompt: Which component is commonly used for internal navigation without a full page reload?
questions.explanation: Link creates client-side navigation for routes handled by React Router.

options.text: Applying active styling based on the current route
Fetching data automatically in every app

questions.explanation: NavLink can expose active state for navigation styling.

questions.prompt: How do you read a route parameter like /users/:userId in a route component?
questions.explanation: useParams reads dynamic segments from the matched route.

questions.prompt: Which are React Router concepts covered in this module? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Nested route UIs are composed with Outlet and can include index routes.
useNavigate lets code navigate in response to events or completed actions.

questions.prompt: Client-side protected routes are a user experience guard, not a replacement for server authorization.
questions.explanation: The server must still enforce access to protected data and actions.

questions.prompt: What is data router awareness about?

options.text: React Router can define loaders/actions for route-based data workflows in newer APIs
Only class components can use routes

questions.explanation: Modern React Router has data APIs that can move some fetching and mutations into route definitions.
